full_text:
There was once a stubborn, wilful child who refused to obey his mother in anything. Whatever she told him to do, he did the opposite, stamping his feet in obstinate defiance and spurning all gentle instruction.

The child fell ill and died, but even in the grave, his stubbornness would not rest. Whenever his little arm was buried beneath the earth, it thrust itself upward through the soil into the open air, refusing to remain peaceful.

The heartbroken mother came to the churchyard, carrying a birch twig. She gently tapped the little hand that reached through the earth, speaking words of maternal discipline and love.

At that loving touch of guidance, the little arm withdrew beneath the soft sod, resting quietly at last beneath the sheltering soil, teaching that the heart finds true peace only when defiance yields to gentle discipline and love.
moral: Stubborn defiance of parental wisdom disturbs the peace of the soul until humility is restored.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Wilful Child variant"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
